posts.caption:
The internet is not only for adults. Young people are already coding, researching, designing, writing, and building online. The goal should be safer access to the open web, not permanent confinement inside a few corporate platforms.
#opensource #safety

author.name: MAPLE OpenSource License for Minors
author.biography: We are creating the world's first SPDX-indexable open source software license dedicated to protecting the intellectual property of minors. By @OpenRockets

posts.caption:
What a young person creates should not automatically drift into systems controlled by giant companies. We want stronger ways for minors to understand, license, and control their own work. Ownership should begin with the creator.

#opensource

author.name: MAPLE OpenSource License for Minors
author.biography: We are creating the world's first SPDX-indexable open source software license dedicated to protecting the intellectual property of minors. By @OpenRockets

posts.caption:
Safety should not mean locking young people inside tiny corporate versions of the internet like @youtube kids. Minors deserve to explore, learn, and build on the real web with strong safety tools, real guidance, and real freedom to be curious.

@openrockets

author.name: MAPLE OpenSource License for Minors
author.biography: We are creating the world's first SPDX-indexable open source software license dedicated to protecting the intellectual property of minors. By @OpenRockets

posts.caption:
A kid in a refugee camp can write code that reaches the world. Their work should not become invisible just because they are young. Intellectual property belongs to young creators too, and the systems around it should recognize them.

#opensource

author.name: MAPLE OpenSource License for Minors
author.biography: We are creating the world's first SPDX-indexable open source software license dedicated to protecting the intellectual property of minors. By @OpenRockets

posts.caption:
Minors create software, art, research, games, and ideas every day. Yet the rules around ownership were mostly built for adults. We are working toward a standard software license designed for minors, so young creators can protect what they build.

@openrockets #opensource #tech

posts.caption:
A 14-year-old can write the code. Own the copyright. Publish the project. And still disappear from the legal record when an adult has to sign.

That is the riddle behind MAPLE 1.0: preserve the minor as author while legal capacity is handled separately.

Among over 1M+ adults tested, only 2% had high creative capacities.
